meta.note: Correcting copy B reproduces copy A exactly, so the corrected list is a redundant duplicate of the frozen list, not new information. Use "quarantined" for the primary analysis; use "corrected" only to test that the fix, not the row deletion, drives any change.
meta.select_by: row_id lists in this file, or cond__diluent__chloroform==1 / cond__diluent__ch3cl==1 for this extractant. A single condition_id names only 14 of the 70 rows.
meta.leakage_warning: The 'corrected' log_D values are computed from copy A's log_D. The two copies sit in different series_id and different condition_id, so unseen_series / unseen_conditions splits can put copy A in train and copy B in test; using 'corrected' under such a split makes a test target a deterministic function of a training target. Use 'corrected' only with an extractant-level split. Never join log_D_corrected or decade_shift_vs_pair in as a feature: both are label-derived.
